independence_caveat: THREE reviewers, each given four card anchors and a rubric and nothing else. Each was explicitly barred from the batch manifest, everything under meoclass1/oral-intelligence/, every AUGUST2026_* file, this record, and the commit history, and each confirmed in its report that it had opened none of them. None saw the producing reasoning, none saw the freeze record, and none was told what verdict was expected. Each was instructed to verify against issuing-body text rather than by finding a second site repeating a claim, and the reports show them doing so - two of the four heaviest findings were established by pulling the IMO resolution PDFs and quoting them.
scope: All 12 produced actions of batch G3 - 11 new cards and 1 enrichment - split 4/4/4 across three reviewers.
outcome: NINE of the twelve cards required fixes; one was returned DO_NOT_PUBLISH and was rewritten rather than patched. 46 edits were applied across 7 files. No card was left live with a known defect, and a second-pass sweep confirmed that no corrected claim survived in any secondary block.
producer_verification_of_findings: Findings were not applied on the reviewer's word. The four heaviest were re-verified against primary sources by the producer before any edit: the HNS status against the IOPP-administered status register; the IGF exclusion against SOLAS II-1/56.4; MSC.132(75) by pulling the resolution from the IMO CDN and reading paragraphs 3 and 5 to 8; and the SOLAS II-1/3-4.2 applicability by pulling MSC.256(84) and reading paragraph 2.1. All four were confirmed exactly as reported.

SOLAS II-1/3-11 requires the CARGO OIL TANKS of crude oil tankers of 5,000 DWT and above to be coated per res. MSC.288(87), or protected by an alternative means or corrosion-resistant material for 25 years per res. MSC.289(87), for ships contracted on or after 1 January 2013. The ballast-tank PSPC is a different standard, MSC.215(82) under SOLAS II-1/3-2. Corrected, with both standards now distinguished.

FINDING: the card implied inert gas is a crude-carrier feature. SOLAS II-2/4.5.5 as amended by MSC.365(93) requires IGS on tankers of 8,000 DWT and above built on or after 1 January 2016 carrying low-flashpoint cargo, which includes modern product tankers. Added.

cards.verdict_basis: PASS after a full rewrite on the AMENDED text of the guidelines. The card was replaced, not patched.
authority_checked: FINDING, and the most serious of the batch: the card answered with the PRE-2002 rule. It was built from res. MSC.35(63) as adopted in 1994, and res. MSC.132(75) of 22 May 2002 amended exactly the paragraphs it relied on - para 3 replaced 'Forward of ship'/'Aft of ship' in 2.2 with 'Non pre-rigged'/'Pre-rigged', para 5 replaced 'aft' with 'pre-rigged' in 3.1.1, para 7 replaced 'forward' with 'non pre-rigged' in 3.1.3, and para 8 replaced 3.1.5 with 'Pre-rigged emergency towing arrangements at both ends of the ship may be accepted.' The producer pulled MSC.132(75) from the IMO CDN and confirmed all four verbatim.

So the times attach to PRE-RIGGED (15 min) and NON PRE-RIGGED (1 h), not to aft and forward, and SOLAS II-1/3-4.1.2.1 requires only that AT LEAST ONE arrangement be pre-rigged - it does not say which end. The card had the old framing in eight blocks including a trap answer that explained the wrong rule.

FINDING: the card asserted 'all ships of 500 GT and above' as the words of the procedures limb. MSC.256(84) was pulled and read: II-1/3-4.2.1 says 'all passenger ships, not later than 1 January 2010; cargo ships constructed on or after 1 January 2010; and cargo ships constructed before 1 January 2010, not later than 1 January 2012.' There is NO gross tonnage in the regulation, and the paraphrase is wrong for passenger ships, which are caught at any size. Rewritten to quote the three dated limbs.

Every NUMBER on the card was verified verbatim against MSC.35(63) and none was wrong - 20,000 dwt, 1,000/2,000 kN at the 50,000 dwt break, working strength one half ultimate, 90 and 30 degrees, pennant 2x freeboard + 50 m, chafing chain 3 m beyond the fairlead, bending ratio 7:1, 15 min and 1 h. The defect was entirely in what the numbers attached to.
MSC.1/Circ.1255/Rev.1 approved at MSC 110 in 2025 - independently verified as real and correctly cited.

cards.verdict_basis: PASS after the clean-agent mechanism was corrected in four blocks.
authority_checked: FINDING, load-bearing: the card said the clean agents that replaced Halon extinguish by breaking the chain reaction, and used that to justify the fourth face. Wrong for both families - halocarbon agents (FM-200, Novec 1230) extinguish predominantly by heat absorption, and inert-gas agents (Inergen, IG-55, IG-100) by oxygen dilution at roughly 35-50 per cent design concentration. Only the bromine-bearing halons were predominantly chain-breakers. Corrected in the 15-second block, the 60-second block, body section 2, body section 3 and the Failures block.

FINDING: 'a CO2 total flooding system... the discharge is also strongly cooling' contradicted the card's own Failures block calling CO2 a smothering agent. Corrected to oxygen dilution, with the soak-time and boundary-cooling consequence stated.

FINDING: SOLAS II-2/4 requires insulation of surfaces above 220 degrees C 'which may be impinged as a result of a fuel system failure'. The card stated the duty unconditionally in two blocks. Qualifier added to both.
21 per cent, about 15 per cent, 8 per cent inert cargo tank atmosphere and 220 degrees C all verified.
The card's own guard - that the tetrahedron is not an IMO instrument and must not be attributed to a convention - was called correct and was left as it stands.

cards.verdict_basis: PASS after the IGF claim, the HNS status and the GC Code date were corrected.
authority_checked: FINDING, currency, and the most consequential on this card: HNS was presented as the applicable regime for a gas cargo. The 2010 HNS Convention is NOT in force. Entry-into-force conditions were met on 29 May 2026 and it enters into force on 29 November 2027; 13 contracting States as at 30 June 2026. Verified by the producer against the official status register. Corrected in five blocks, and the card now names the instrument WITH its status and says what governs until then.

FINDING: 'IGC governs the cargo, IGF governs the fuel - both are live on a gas carrier burning boil-off' is wrong. SOLAS II-1/56.4 expressly excludes gas carriers using their own cargoes as fuel from the IGF Code where they comply with the IGC Code; that use is governed by IGC Chapter 16. Verified independently by the producer. Corrected in three blocks.
FINDING: the GC Code applies from 31 October 1976 (res. A.328(IX)), not 1 July 1976. Corrected in two blocks, with A.329(IX) added for the Existing Ship Code.

FINDING: the Tanker Safety Guide (Liquefied Gas) is published by the International Chamber of Shipping, not by SIGTTO. Corrected in two places - and it mattered here, because the card's own point is that industry guidance must be attributed accurately.

cards.verdict_basis: PASS after the 2017 date and the SC140 attribution were corrected.
authority_checked: FINDING: the card dated the secondary means of venting requirement to tankers constructed on or after 1 January 2017, in the body and in Key Numbers. Wrong as a trigger for the requirement: SOLAS II-2/11.6.3.2 has required a secondary means for far longer. What res. MSC.392(95) added for ships built from 1 January 2017 is the further capability to prevent over- or under-pressure on damage to, or inadvertent closing of, the means of isolation. This sentence PRE-DATES batch G3 and was corrected in place because the G3 enrichment restructured the section containing it.

FINDING, and this one was authored by this batch: the enrichment cited IACS UI SC140 in support of the argument that a P/V breaker on the IG main will not serve as the secondary means. SC140 Rev.3 said the OPPOSITE - it accepted exactly that. The position changed with MSC.392(95). The citation now names the revision problem explicitly.
FINDING: the alarm-setting convention was attributed to the regulation; it comes from SC140. The regulation requires only an alarm activated by detection of over- or under-pressure. Re-attributed.

VERIFIED CORRECT and unchanged: the two permitted forms of secondary means, and that the pressure-sensor option is conditional on a full-flow P/V valve being the primary means for that tank - which is the limb the enrichment was written to add.
II-2/4.5.3.4.1.3, 4.5.3.3, 11.6, 11.6.3.2, 4.5.5 and FSS Code Ch.15 all verified correct including sub-paragraph numbering; 6 m, 10 m and 2 m verified.

batch_level_findings: THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING IS ABOUT METHOD, NOT CONTENT. QB1_K#q10 was written from a primary source - the IMO's own PDF of resolution MSC.35(63) - and was still wrong, because that PDF is the resolution AS ADOPTED in 1994 and MSC.132(75) amended it in 2002. Reading a primary source is not the same as reading the CURRENT text of a primary source, and the IMO Index of IMO Resolutions serves the former. Recorded as a reusable trap: an IMO resolution PDF carries no forward pointer to its own amendments.

The IGC/IGF 'both codes apply' error found in QB8_D#q3 was NOT introduced by this batch. It is pre-existing in QB8_D#q1, in that card's CE tip and trap block, and in the page cheat sheet. The G3 card repeated an error the bank already held. Raised as OPEN-G1-012; the batch's own card is now correct, which means the file currently disagrees with itself until that correction lands.

Two of the corrected statements were pre-existing rather than authored here: the QB8_A#q7 sentence dating the secondary means of venting to 1 January 2017, and the QB8_D IGC/IGF claim. The first was corrected in place because the G3 enrichment restructured the very section it sits in; the second was corrected only inside the G3 card.
No card in this batch names an examiner, before or after review. Examiner relationships stay at 958.

Every reviewer independently checked the 15-second block, the 60-second block, the body, the Regulatory References box, the CE Oral Tip and the collapsed deep-dive separately. Three of the nine defective cards had a defect that was CONSISTENT across every block, which is the case a spot-check would miss entirely.
